title: $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ is the limit of its finite levels
statement:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with ring of integers $\cO_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$, and
let $X$ be a scheme. For $n\ge1$ let $(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ be the constant sheaf of rings on
$X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with value the finite ring $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$, and let
$(\cO_E/\pi_E^{n+1})_X\to(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ be the reduction maps.

1. For a finite set $T$, the constant sheaf $T_X$ is represented by the $X$-scheme
   $\coprod_TX$. For the profinite set $\cO_E=\varprojlim_n\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ the pro-étale
   $X$-scheme
   $$
   X[\cO_E]=\varprojlim_n\coprod_{\cO_E/\pi_E^n}X
   $$
   of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] represents $\varprojlim_n(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ (limit
   of sheaves of sets).
2. The underlying sheaf of sets of $\cO_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\cO_E}$ is represented by
   $X[\cO_E]$.
3. Consequently there is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves of rings
   $\cO_{E,X}\cong\varprojlim_n(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, the limit being taken in sheaves of rings
   (equivalently, in sheaves of sets, with the induced ring structure).

proof.text: Use proEtaleFiniteConstantRepresentableIso and the finite test-object comparison to construct the natural finite representation. Construct the positive tower cone on the integers by the topological ring identification with compatible residues. Prove its universal property coordinatewise, then preserve it through the locally constant ring right adjoint, Spec and relative base change.

Commute the abelian inverse image with forgetting, using uniqueness of left adjoints and the sheafification/Kan extension comparison. Left Kan extension sends the represented condensed integers to the represented relative test object. For the completion, finite comparison naturality identifies the two diagrams; forgetting preserves limits and Yoneda preserves the relative cone, so uniqueness of limits gives the completed representation. Prove the canonical pullback representation sends unit sections to X[f] using the unit equation for left-adjoint uniqueness and the Yoneda adjunct. Prove the completed representation sends every finite projection to composition with the reduction by the inverse comparison equation for limiting cones.

Apply the ring-lifting lemma to the two explicitly normalized underlying representations and the genuine reduction cone. It supplies an additive sheaf morphism whose underlying map is their specified composite, preserving multiplication and one. This underlying map is an isomorphism. Forgetting abelian groups and including sheaves both reflect isomorphisms, so the additive morphism is invertible and its inverse is a monoid homomorphism. Evaluate its underlying-map equation on a unit section; use the proved pullback-unit formula and completed inverse-projection formula to prove the required normalization. For uniqueness apply the point adjunction, evaluate at every profinite test object, and use joint injectivity of finite ring-limit projections, cancelling the finite representation isomorphisms.
